headline: High-risk pair: LightAgent’s broad egress/MCP and browser tooling can leak or misapply outputs when paired with Opik’s REST-facing observability flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can run browsers, use MCP, and accept stdin/stdout or SSE/API inputs, so attacker-controlled content could reach its instruction channel. Opik exposes a REST API and is an observability/evaluation system, so if its outputs are bridged into LightAgent without provenance checks, prompt injection is plausible. The shared channel is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are copied into LightAgent prompts or MCP payloads without sanitization
IF browser-fetched content is fed from LightAgent into Opik as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from Opik outputs
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages
Require a human review step before LightAgent executes Opik-derived text
Restrict browser-scraped content to quoted excerpts only
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and provenance filtering at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent explicitly touches user conversations, long-term memory, trace data, tool calls/results, and secrets, while also having broad network egress. Opik is a REST API observability tool, so if shared workspace or logs are forwarded into it, sensitive data can flow out. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default integrations, but the exact workspace sharing is not documented.
conditions: IF LightAgent logs or traces are exported to Opik by default
IF either agent is configured to send full tool results or memory into the shared observability pipeline
mitigations: Redact secrets and memory before export
Limit Opik ingestion to metadata-only fields
Turn off verbose tracing for sensitive runs
Separate credentials used by the two agents
requires-engineering: add field-level allowlists for exported payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and can spawn subprocesses, while Opik is a REST API consumer/producer with no write privileges or OAuth scopes listed. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because B lacks write-capability evidence.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or git repo
IF an external orchestrator grants Opik write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Run Opik read-only against exported traces
Avoid shared git or filesystem mounts
Document ownership of any mutable resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can emit tool results, provenance metadata, and workflow state, and Opik is an evaluation/observability system that may consume those outputs. If Opik treats LightAgent output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect evaluations or downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from their roles, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Opik ingests LightAgent outputs without verification
IF LightAgent-generated facts are used as ground truth in evaluation or automation
mitigations: Add a verification step before Opik accepts LightAgent outputs
Mark LightAgent outputs as untrusted by default
Compare outputs against source artifacts before scoring
Log disagreements for manual review
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and confidence thresholds

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles secrets and user conversations, while Opik’s profile shows no special residency or certification constraints. The main compliance concern is retention/logging mismatch if LightAgent data is exported into Opik, but the profile does not show a direct residency violation. Only LightAgent is cited because the issue is its sensitive data handling; Opik lacks documented compliance constraints.
conditions: IF LightAgent exports conversations or secrets into Opik logs
IF retention settings differ between LightAgent traces and Opik storage
mitigations: Disable retention of sensitive traces
Mask secrets before export
Set short log retention windows
Review data-processing notices for exported fields
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
